title: How to Make AI Work for Workers
excerpt: How to make AI work for workers
content_html:
Over the past 40 years, the emergence of digital technology led to a surge in automation, amplifying inequality even as it increased productivity. Economic growth continued, but it enriched only some groups while punishing many others. This not only precipitated a collapse of shared prosperity; it also exacerbated the crisis of liberal democracy that’s upending much of the developed world.

Now generative AI is poised to supercharge the inequities of the past four decades. But this isn’t inevitable. A society-wide effort will be required to avoid the mistakes that were made during the advent of digital technology. That will mean redirecting AI development so that it benefits workers instead of replacing them. I call this “pro-worker AI”: models that expand the capabilities of workers, give them new tasks, and make them more productive.

From a technological perspective, it’s entirely feasible—and in some cases already proven. Such a transformation won’t happen on its own, and it won’t be simple. But there are ways to jump-start it.

We’ve known for some time that AI can enhance workers’ skills instead of rendering them useless. The computer scientist J. C. R. Licklider saw this back in 1960, when he predicted that computers would one day augment human cognition by providing workers with highly processed, context-sensitive information. For the next six decades, digital technology was not up to that task. The internet represented a breakthrough in collecting and storing information, but retrieving it remained a challenge. Although search engines could quickly yield countless results, humans were the ones who had to process them, sequentially and slowly.

From the July 1945 issue: As we may think

Now generative AI has fulfilled Licklider’s prophecy. It can find the most relevant answers to a query and summarize them almost instantaneously, in digestible form. It can process technical information and furnish precise guidance for complicated tasks performed under specific conditions. This kind of information retrieval and provision forms the basis of pro-worker AI. If widely adopted, it could increase wages, employment, and productivity all at the same time, restoring the link between productivity growth and good jobs that the past four decades have severed.

Pro-worker AI would serve far more people than just knowledge workers who need to draft slide decks or emails. Consider electricians, who are in high demand across many industries. You don’t need a large language model that can write sonnets to be able to troubleshoot electrical equipment; you need specialized models trained on niche, high-quality data. These are the hallmarks of pro-worker AI. Facing ever more sophisticated equipment and grids, electricians could benefit from an AI tool that draws on a targeted knowledge base, past use cases, and site-specific inputs—sensor data, photographs, written reports—to help them identify problems with machinery or circuitry. Indeed, a global company is already developing a set of products like this for a range of field technicians.

Pro-worker AI could boost productivity across other service industries, too. In education, a model trained on relevant curricular material might allow teachers to spot patterns in test results and tailor lesson plans for particular groups of students who tend to make the same mistakes. This is one of many ways that AI could make education more cost-effective and personalized, which could drive up demand for teachers and bolster their wages.

Perhaps most important, pro-worker AI could create good service jobs for workers who aren’t college educated, and thus begin to uproot the inequality that has been entrenched in the postindustrial economy. In the health-care industry, for example, specially trained models could enable lower-skilled laborers to perform a broader range of tasks, particularly those that rely more on physical exertion and social interaction than on medical expertise.

The promises of pro-worker AI won’t be realized, however, unless it receives more attention and investment. This will require a dramatic shift in how all parts of society—governments, corporations, investors, workers—think about AI.

In Silicon Valley today, most funding chases automation. This isn’t entirely surprising. Automation can be lucrative for both managers and shareholders because it reduces payroll and decreases dependence on organized labor. More broadly, AI models that act and sound like us—instead of those that support us—attract a disproportionate amount of hype. “Reaching human parity” has become a key metric of success in Silicon Valley.

At the same time, the global race for AI supremacy largely centers on artificial general intelligence, which would in theory be able to take over human labor across all sectors, including white-collar cognitive work and the nonroutine tasks that skilled blue-collar and craft workers perform. Even models that don’t meet the AGI threshold could eliminate an untold number of jobs. The few people lucky enough to claim the remaining tasks in the economy would lose substantial wages.

From the March 2026 issue: America isn’t ready for what AI will do to jobs

Several policies could begin to shift Silicon Valley’s attention toward pro-worker AI. Starting at the international level, the United States and Europe should create AI agencies that can generate incentives—such as grant programs or public competitions—for technologists to develop models that are designed to expand workers’ capabilities.

A simpler fix involves the tax code. Tax laws in many industrialized economies encourage far too much automation. In the United States, for example, labor income is taxed significantly more than capital income. If a business pays a worker $100, it will have to hand over as much as $30 in tax and spending obligations. But paying $100 for automation equipment leads to a tax burden of less than $5, a number that has dropped as companies have been allowed to write off more spending on digital infrastructure. For the most part, this tax asymmetry triggers only mediocre productivity gains. In fact, even when automated labor is less productive than human workers, a company may well make money by automating.

To a certain extent, employers’ preference for automation is unavoidable. For one thing, companies need to cover health insurance for humans and not for machines. But removing these distortions in the tax system would create a more level playing field for workers, as well as for the development of pro-worker AI models.

Part of the promise of pro-worker AI is to create new tasks, which in many cases will demand that laborers learn new skills. As such, society will need to invest in worker training. By “training” here, I’m not referring to the unrealistic goal of turning coal miners into computer programmers. Rather, training should aim to allow workers, including manual and craft workers, to boost their existing expertise. The introduction of AI to the workforce may continuously change which skills are in demand, so training will have to be adaptive and emphasize flexibility. Pro-worker AI itself could play a role, helping update training programs just as it can help teachers revise lesson plans.

Redirecting technological change toward pro-worker AI will also involve even more herculean undertakings. Chief among them is reducing the dominance of technology monopolies, which have an outsize effect on AI development. They’re using it not only to push the technology toward automation and AGI, but also to discourage innovation by forcing out new companies that have unorthodox, and potentially disruptive, ideas. Creating a more competitive environment would open greater space for pro-worker AI. This can be achieved by enforcing existing antitrust laws, which have rarely been applied in tech. It may also require limiting Silicon Valley’s considerable power of persuasion, for example by fostering more and better-funded independent media.

A stronger labor movement would help too. Rather than resist AI, unions should become advocates of a pro-worker AI agenda. Merely bargaining for higher wages won’t be enough: Most companies will respond to demands for higher wages by simply choosing more automation. Instead, unions will have to build the case that corporate investments in pro-worker AI can benefit both labor and management, making the former more productive and the latter more profitable.

At stake is a core tenet of the liberal economic order: that jobs and wage growth remain available to workers of different skills and backgrounds. The past 40 years have jeopardized this promise. But they have also produced new, capable technologies—most important AI—that can help workers rather than sideline them. First we have to decide that automation won’t be the north star of the AI age.

This essay has been adapted from Daron Acemoglu’s new book, What Happened to Liberal Democracy?

By

Daron Acemoglu

sentences.zh: 更广泛地说，行为和声音与我们相似的人工智能模型——而不是那些支持我们的模型——吸引了不成比例的炒作。

sentences.en: “Reaching human parity” has become a key metric of success in Silicon Valley.
sentences.zh: “达到人类平等”已成为硅谷成功的关键衡量标准。

blocks.html_en: At the same time, the global race for AI supremacy largely centers on artificial general intelligence, which would in theory be able to take over human labor across all sectors, including white-collar cognitive work and the nonroutine tasks that skilled blue-collar and craft workers perform. Even models that don’t meet the AGI threshold could eliminate an untold number of jobs. The few people lucky enough to claim the remaining tasks in the economy would lose substantial wages.

blocks.html_en: Several policies could begin to shift Silicon Valley’s attention toward pro-worker AI. Starting at the international level, the United States and Europe should create AI agencies that can generate incentives—such as grant programs or public competitions—for technologists to develop models that are designed to expand workers’ capabilities.

sentences.en: Several policies could begin to shift Silicon Valley’s attention toward pro-worker AI.
sentences.zh: 多项政策可能会开始将硅谷的注意力转向有利于工人的人工智能。

sentences.en: Starting at the international level, the United States and Europe should create AI agencies that can generate incentives—such as grant programs or public competitions—for technologists to develop models that are designed to expand workers’ capabilities.

blocks.html_en: A simpler fix involves the tax code. Tax laws in many industrialized economies encourage far too much automation. In the United States, for example, labor income is taxed significantly more than capital income. If a business pays a worker $100, it will have to hand over as much as $30 in tax and spending obligations. But paying $100 for automation equipment leads to a tax burden of less than $5, a number that has dropped as companies have been allowed to write off more spending on digital infrastructure. For the most part, this tax asymmetry triggers only mediocre productivity gains. In fact, even when automated labor is less productive than human workers, a company may well make money by automating.

sentences.en: A simpler fix involves the tax code.
sentences.zh: 一个更简单的解决方案涉及税法。

sentences.en: Tax laws in many industrialized economies encourage far too much automation.
sentences.zh: 许多工业化经济体的税法鼓励过多的自动化。

sentences.en: In the United States, for example, labor income is taxed significantly more than capital income.
sentences.zh: 例如，在美国，对劳动收入的征税远高于对资本收入的征税。

sentences.en: If a business pays a worker $100, it will have to hand over as much as $30 in tax and spending obligations.
sentences.zh: 如果企业向员工支付 100 美元，则必须缴纳高达 30 美元的税收和支出义务。

sentences.en: But paying $100 for automation equipment leads to a tax burden of less than $5, a number that has dropped as companies have been allowed to write off more spending on digital infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 但支付 100 美元购买自动化设备，税负不到 5 美元，随着公司被允许冲销更多数字基础设施支出，这一数字已经下降。

sentences.en: In fact, even when automated labor is less productive than human workers, a company may well make money by automating.
sentences.zh: 事实上，即使自动化劳动力的生产力低于人类工人，公司也很可能通过自动化赚钱。

blocks.html_en: To a certain extent, employers’ preference for automation is unavoidable. For one thing, companies need to cover health insurance for humans and not for machines. But removing these distortions in the tax system would create a more level playing field for workers, as well as for the development of pro-worker AI models.

sentences.en: To a certain extent, employers’ preference for automation is unavoidable.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，雇主对自动化的偏好是不可避免的。

sentences.en: For one thing, companies need to cover health insurance for humans and not for machines.
sentences.zh: 一方面，公司需要为人类而非机器提供健康保险。

sentences.en: But removing these distortions in the tax system would create a more level playing field for workers, as well as for the development of pro-worker AI models.
sentences.zh: 但消除税收体系中的这些扭曲将为工人创造一个更加公平的竞争环境，也有利于有利于工人的人工智能模型的开发。

blocks.html_en: Part of the promise of pro-worker AI is to create new tasks, which in many cases will demand that laborers learn new skills. As such, society will need to invest in worker training. By “training” here, I’m not referring to the unrealistic goal of turning coal miners into computer programmers. Rather, training should aim to allow workers, including manual and craft workers, to boost their existing expertise. The introduction of AI to the workforce may continuously change which skills are in demand, so training will have to be adaptive and emphasize flexibility. Pro-worker AI itself could play a role, helping update training programs just as it can help teachers revise lesson plans.

sentences.en: Part of the promise of pro-worker AI is to create new tasks, which in many cases will demand that laborers learn new skills.
sentences.zh: 支持工人的人工智能的部分承诺是创造新任务，在许多情况下，这将要求工人学习新技能。

sentences.en: As such, society will need to invest in worker training.
sentences.zh: 因此，社会需要投资于工人培训。

sentences.en: By “training” here, I’m not referring to the unrealistic goal of turning coal miners into computer programmers.
sentences.zh: 这里的“培训”并不是指将煤矿工人变成计算机程序员的不切实际的目标。

sentences.en: Rather, training should aim to allow workers, including manual and craft workers, to boost their existing expertise.
sentences.zh: 相反，培训的目的应该是让工人，包括体力工人和手工艺工人，提高他们现有的专业知识。

sentences.en: The introduction of AI to the workforce may continuously change which skills are in demand, so training will have to be adaptive and emphasize flexibility.
sentences.zh: 将人工智能引入劳动力可能会不断改变所需的技能，因此培训必须具有适应性并强调灵活性。

sentences.en: Pro-worker AI itself could play a role, helping update training programs just as it can help teachers revise lesson plans.
sentences.zh: 支持工人的人工智能本身可以发挥作用，帮助更新培训计划，就像帮助教师修改课程计划一样。

blocks.html_en: Redirecting technological change toward pro-worker AI will also involve even more herculean undertakings. Chief among them is reducing the dominance of technology monopolies, which have an outsize effect on AI development. They’re using it not only to push the technology toward automation and AGI, but also to discourage innovation by forcing out new companies that have unorthodox, and potentially disruptive, ideas. Creating a more competitive environment would open greater space for pro-worker AI. This can be achieved by enforcing existing antitrust laws, which have rarely been applied in tech. It may also require limiting Silicon Valley’s considerable power of persuasion, for example by fostering more and better-funded independent media.

sentences.en: Redirecting technological change toward pro-worker AI will also involve even more herculean undertakings.
sentences.zh: 将技术变革转向有利于工人的人工智能也将涉及更加艰巨的任务。

sentences.en: Chief among them is reducing the dominance of technology monopolies, which have an outsize effect on AI development.
sentences.zh: 其中最主要的是减少技术垄断的主导地位，这对人工智能的发展有着巨大的影响。

sentences.en: They’re using it not only to push the technology toward automation and AGI, but also to discourage innovation by forcing out new companies that have unorthodox, and potentially disruptive, ideas.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅利用它来推动技术走向自动化和通用人工智能，还通过驱逐拥有非正统且可能具有颠覆性想法的新公司来阻碍创新。

sentences.zh: 创造一个更具竞争性的环境将为有利于工人的人工智能开辟更大的空间。

sentences.zh: 这可以通过执行现有的反垄断法来实现，但这些法很少应用于科技领域。

sentences.zh: 它还可能需要限制硅谷的巨大说服力，例如通过培育更多、资金更充足的独立媒体。

blocks.html_en: A stronger labor movement would help too. Rather than resist AI, unions should become advocates of a pro-worker AI agenda. Merely bargaining for higher wages won’t be enough: Most companies will respond to demands for higher wages by simply choosing more automation. Instead, unions will have to build the case that corporate investments in pro-worker AI can benefit both labor and management, making the former more productive and the latter more profitable.

sentences.en: A stronger labor movement would help too.
sentences.zh: 更强大的劳工运动也会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Rather than resist AI, unions should become advocates of a pro-worker AI agenda.
sentences.zh: 工会不应该抵制人工智能，而应该成为有利于工人的人工智能议程的倡导者。

sentences.en: Merely bargaining for higher wages won’t be enough: Most companies will respond to demands for higher wages by simply choosing more automation.
sentences.zh: 仅仅讨价还价是不够的：大多数公司会通过选择更多的自动化来应对更高工资的要求。

sentences.en: Instead, unions will have to build the case that corporate investments in pro-worker AI can benefit both labor and management, making the former more productive and the latter more profitable.
sentences.zh: 相反，工会必须证明企业对有利于工人的人工智能的投资可以使劳工和管理层受益，使前者更具生产力，后者更有利可图。

blocks.html_en: At stake is a core tenet of the liberal economic order: that jobs and wage growth remain available to workers of different skills and backgrounds. The past 40 years have jeopardized this promise. But they have also produced new, capable technologies—most important AI—that can help workers rather than sideline them. First we have to decide that automation won’t be the north star of the AI age.

content_html_zh:
过去 40 年来，数字技术的出现导致自动化程度激增，在提高生产力的同时也加剧了不平等。 经济增长仍在继续，但它只让一些群体富裕起来，同时也惩罚了许多其他群体。 这不仅导致了共同繁荣的崩溃；而且还导致了共同繁荣的崩溃。它还加剧了正在颠覆许多发达国家的自由民主危机。

现在，生成式人工智能有望加剧过去四十年的不平等现象。 但这并非不可避免。 需要全社会的努力来避免数字技术出现期间所犯的错误。 这将意味着重新调整人工智能的发展方向，使其惠及工人而不是取代他们。 我将其称为“支持工人的人工智能”：扩展工人能力、赋予他们新任务并提高他们生产力的模型。

从技术角度来看，这是完全可行的——并且在某些情况下已经得到证明。 这种转变不会自行发生，也不会简单。 但有一些方法可以启动它。

一段时间以来，我们已经知道人工智能可以提高工人的技能，而不是让他们变得毫无用处。 计算机科学家 J. C. R。 Licklider 早在 1960 年就看到了这一点，当时他预测计算机有一天会通过为工人提供经过高度处理的上下文敏感信息来增强人类认知。 在接下来的六年里，数字技术无法胜任这项任务。 互联网代表了信息收集和存储方面的突破，但检索信息仍然是一个挑战。 尽管搜索引擎可以快速产生无数结果，但人类必须顺序且缓慢地处理它们。

摘自 1945 年 7 月号：正如我们所想

现在生成式人工智能已经实现了利克莱德的预言。 它可以找到与查询最相关的答案，并几乎立即以易于理解的形式总结它们。 它可以处理技术信息并为特定条件下执行的复杂任务提供精确指导。 这种信息检索和提供构成了亲工人人工智能的基础。 如果得到广泛采用，它可以同时提高工资、就业和生产率，恢复过去四十年来被切断的生产​​率增长和良好就业之间的联系。

支持工人的人工智能将服务于更多的人，而不仅仅是需要起草幻灯片或电子邮件的知识工人。 以电工为例，许多行业对电工的需求量很大。 您不需要一个可以编写十四行诗的大型语言模型来对电气设备进行故障排除；您需要针对利基、高质量数据进行训练的专门模型。 这些都是支持工人的人工智能的标志。 面对越来越复杂的设备和电网，电工可以从人工智能工具中受益，该工具利用有针对性的知识库、过去的用例和特定地点的输入（传感器数据、照片、书面报告）来帮助他们识别机械或电路的问题。 事实上，一家跨国公司已经在为一系列现场技术人员开发一套类似的产品。

有利于工人的人工智能也可以提高其他服务行业的生产力。 在教育领域，根据相关课程材料训练的模型可以让教师发现测试结果中的模式，并为容易犯同样错误的特定学生群体量身定制课程计划。 这是人工智能使教育更具成本效益和个性化的众多方式之一，这可能会增加对教师的需求并提高他们的工资。

也许最重要的是，有利于工人的人工智能可以为未受过大学教育的工人创造良好的服务工作，从而开始根除后工业经济中根深蒂固的不平等现象。 例如，在医疗保健行业，经过专门训练的模型可以使低技能劳动者能够执行更广泛的任务，特别是那些更多依赖体力消耗和社会互动而不是医疗专业知识的任务。

然而，除非得到更多的关注和投资，有利于工人的人工智能的承诺将无法实现。 这需要社会各方——政府、企业、投资者、工人——对人工智能的看法发生巨大转变。

在当今的硅谷，大多数资金都追逐自动化。 这并不完全令人惊讶。 自动化对于管理者和股东来说都是有利可图的，因为它减少了工资并减少了对有组织劳动力的依赖。 更广泛地说，行为和声音与我们相似的人工智能模型——而不是那些支持我们的模型——吸引了不成比例的炒作。 “达到人类平等”已成为硅谷成功的关键衡量标准。

与此同时，全球人工智能霸主地位的争夺主要集中在通用人工智能上，理论上，通用人工智能将能够接管所有部门的人类劳动力，包括白领认知工作以及熟练蓝领和手工艺工人执行的非常规任务。 即使不符合 AGI 阈值的模型也可能会消除无数的工作岗位。 少数有幸声称经济中剩余任务的人将损失大量工资。

摘自 2026 年 3 月号：美国尚未准备好应对人工智能对就业的影响

多项政策可能会开始将硅谷的注意力转向有利于工人的人工智能。 从国际层面开始，美国和欧洲应该创建人工智能机构，为技术人员提供激励措施（例如资助计划或公共竞赛），以开发旨在扩展工人能力的模型。

一个更简单的解决方案涉及税法。 许多工业化经济体的税法鼓励过多的自动化。 例如，在美国，对劳动收入的征税远高于对资本收入的征税。 如果企业向员工支付 100 美元，则必须缴纳高达 30 美元的税收和支出义务。 但支付 100 美元购买自动化设备，税负不到 5 美元，随着公司被允许冲销更多数字基础设施支出，这一数字已经下降。 在大多数情况下，这种税收不对称只会带来平庸的生产率增长。 事实上，即使自动化劳动力的生产力低于人类工人，公司也很可能通过自动化赚钱。

在某种程度上，雇主对自动化的偏好是不可避免的。 一方面，公司需要为人类而非机器提供健康保险。 但消除税收体系中的这些扭曲将为工人创造一个更加公平的竞争环境，也有利于有利于工人的人工智能模型的开发。

支持工人的人工智能的部分承诺是创造新任务，在许多情况下，这将要求工人学习新技能。 因此，社会需要投资于工人培训。 这里的“培训”并不是指将煤矿工人变成计算机程序员的不切实际的目标。 相反，培训的目的应该是让工人，包括体力工人和手工艺工人，提高他们现有的专业知识。 将人工智能引入劳动力可能会不断改变所需的技能，因此培训必须具有适应性并强调灵活性。 支持工人的人工智能本身可以发挥作用，帮助更新培训计划，就像帮助教师修改课程计划一样。

将技术变革转向有利于工人的人工智能也将涉及更加艰巨的任务。 其中最主要的是减少技术垄断的主导地位，这对人工智能的发展有着巨大的影响。 他们不仅利用它来推动技术走向自动化和通用人工智能，还通过驱逐拥有非正统且可能具有颠覆性想法的新公司来阻碍创新。 创造一个更具竞争性的环境将为有利于工人的人工智能开辟更大的空间。 这可以通过执行现有的反垄断法来实现，但这些法很少应用于科技领域。 它还可能需要限制硅谷的巨大说服力，例如通过培育更多、资金更充足的独立媒体。

更强大的劳工运动也会有所帮助。 工会不应该抵制人工智能，而应该成为有利于工人的人工智能议程的倡导者。 仅仅讨价还价是不够的：大多数公司会通过选择更多的自动化来应对更高工资的要求。 相反，工会必须证明企业对有利于工人的人工智能的投资可以使劳工和管理层受益，使前者更具生产力，后者更有利可图。

自由经济秩序的核心原则至关重要：不同技能和背景的工人仍然可以获得工作和工资增长。 过去的 40 年已经危及了这一承诺。 但他们也创造了新的、有能力的技术——最重要的是人工智能——可以帮助工人而不是让他们边缘化。 首先，我们必须确定自动化不会成为人工智能时代的北极星。

本文改编自达龙·阿西莫格鲁的新书《自由民主发生了什么？

By
